definitions.explanation: Japan's largest dragonfly, about ten centimetres long, black with yellow bands and bright green eyes. It patrols streams and forest paths in summer, and catching one is a classic childhood thrill. Usually written in katakana; the kanji spelling is {鬼蜻蜓|おにやんま}.

examples.japanese: オニヤンマ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{飛|と}んでいる→飛ぶ：00759_tobu⟧。
examples.english: A golden-ringed dragonfly is flying around.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ころ、⟦{網|あみ}→網：22587_ami⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧オニヤンマ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{捕|つか}まえた→捕まえる：01214_tsukamaeru⟧。
examples.english: When I was a child, I caught a golden-ringed dragonfly with a net.

examples.japanese: オニヤンマ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{日本最大|にほんさいだい}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧トンボで、⟦{小川|おがわ}→小川：06695_ogawa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{上|うえ}→上：00682_ue⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{行|い}っ⟦たり→たり：33215_tari⟧{来|き}⟦たり→たり：33215_tari⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The golden-ringed dragonfly is Japan's largest dragonfly and flies back and forth over small streams.

notes:
オニ (⟦{鬼|おに}→鬼：02184_oni⟧, ogre) marks it as the giant of the ヤンマ, the big darner dragonflies. Because it hunts other insects, plastic オニヤンマ figures are sold to clip on hats and bags in the hope of keeping flies and wasps away.
